Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with several days of burning on urination, increased urinary frequency, and lower abdominal ache; pink urine today; suspected urinary tract infection/cystitis. Plans include urine testing and empiric antibiotics with follow-up if not improved.
- No fever or systemic symptoms reported. Relevant history includes IBS and use of combined oral contraceptive pill; recent unprotected intercourse reported; cannabis use once. Counseling and monitoring provided with clear follow-up plan.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Suspected urinary tract infection / cystitis.
- Timeline and symptoms: Onset about 4–7 days ago; burning/pain with urination; increased urinary frequency; lower abdominal ache mainly with voiding; pink urine observed today; no frank red blood reported.
- Systems review: No fever, vomiting, or back pain; bowels IBS-related with variable bowel habits noted but no new GI symptoms.
- Social history/medications/exam: 19-year-old student living in uni halls; on combined oral contraceptive pill; IBS med started with M; occasional cannabis use; no vaginal discharge reported; no physical exam findings documented.
- Differential diagnoses considered: UTI/cystitis primarily; other urinary or gynecologic sources not indicated by history.
- Specialist/allied health review: none noted.

Issue 2:
- Pregnancy risk assessment / contraception considerations.
- Timeline and symptoms: On combined OCP; last menstrual period two weeks ago; reported unprotected intercourse approximately 1–2 weeks ago.
- Systems review: No pregnancy symptoms described.
- Social history/medications/exam: On combined pill; no current sexual activity; not pregnant as per history (not explicitly stated but pregnancy risk discussed by clinician).
- Plan/management: Noted for counseling; no testing ordered at this visit beyond urine testing for infection.
- Specialist/allied health review: none noted.

Issue 3:
- Chronic irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with variable bowel habits.
- Timeline and symptoms: Known history of IBS; no new bowel symptoms reported beyond baseline variability.
- Systems review: IBS-related bowel habit variability described; no acute GI symptoms.
- Social history/medications/exam: Takes IBS medication starting with M; no other GI red flags.
- Plan/management: No specific IBS treatment changes documented at this visit.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill (name not specified) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- IBS medication starting with M (name not documented) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol for pain — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Antibiotics discussed as options: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin for 3 days (exact choice not yet specified).

Allergies:
- Clindamycin (antibiotic) — documented allergy.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).

Social History:
- Lives in university halls with a flatmate.
- Age 19; English studies; university student.
- Smokes: not a smoker; cannabis use once (first time) about 1.5 weeks ago.
- Alcohol: drinks socially, occasionally.
- Sexual activity: not currently sexually active; long-term boyfriend; last unprotected intercourse about 1–2 weeks ago.
- Menstrual: last period two weeks ago.

Preventative History:
- Not documented in the transcript (no cervical screening, immunizations, or other routine preventive care details provided).

Physical Examination:
- Not performed at this visit (no vital signs recorded; no physical exam findings documented).

Plan:
- Urine sample: arrange for patient to drop off a sample at a practice today for lab testing.
- Start antibiotics for presumed UTI: options of Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin for 3 days; specific choice to be determined.
- Hydration: encourage increased fluid intake.
- Analgesia: Paracetamol for pain as needed.
- Follow-up: return in one week if symptoms do not improve; reassess then.
- Warning signs: contact the clinic if fever, back pain, vomiting occur.

  - Urine test results not yet available at the time of the visit.
  - Specific antibiotic chosen and dosing instructions not documented.
  - Vaccination status and other preventive services not provided.
  - Full medication reconciliation (dose/route/frequency) for all listed meds not documented.

- Internal conflicts:
  - Onset timeline inconsistent in the transcript (initially “a few days” and “three days,” then “about just under a week”). Conflict noted: timeline ambiguity around symptom onset.
